# Champions of the Future

## Disambiguation and Historical Context

The term "Champions of the Future" refers to multiple distinct entities across different domains, requiring careful disambiguation to accurately address the subject of this report. The primary subject of this analysis is an international karting promotion series organized by the RGMMC Group , . This modern series must be clearly differentiated from two other notable programs sharing a similar name. The most prominent of these is the "Young Champions of the Earth," a prize awarded by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) to individuals aged 18–30 who develop innovative solutions for planetary sustainability . UNEP explicitly uses the branding 'Young Champions of the Earth' and does not utilize the exact title 'Champions of the Future' for any program, confirming no institutional overlap exists between the UN initiative and the motorsport series . Furthermore, a historical British karting championship also bore the name "Champions of the Future." Founded in 1995 by McLaren Formula One team boss Ron Dennis, Mercedes Motorsport chief Norbert Haug, and kart manufacturer Martin Hines, this earlier series aimed to provide a clear pathway for young British talent into Formula One and other upper echelons of motorsport . While both the modern and historical series share a similar overarching goal of talent development, they are separate entities with distinct founders, operational periods, and organizational structures. The modern Champions of the Future series, promoted by RGMMC, was officially launched in 2020 and has since established itself as a significant developmental platform within the sport of karting .

The contemporary Champions of the Future series was founded in 2020 by the Racing Group Middle East Motorsport Company (RGMMC), a global leader in international karting promotion , . Its inception marked a strategic entry into the competitive world of karting promotion, aiming to create a professional pathway for elite motorsport talent . The series was designed from the outset to align with the highest levels of international motorsport governance, securing sanctioning from FIA Karting (CIK-FIA) , . This affiliation provided immediate credibility and positioned the series within the official framework of global karting competitions, alongside major championships such as the FIA Karting World Championship and the FIA Karting European Championship . However, the inaugural season faced significant disruption due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The first season, which was originally scheduled for May–June 2020, was delayed and ultimately cancelled . This setback did not derail the project, and the series made its long-awaited debut on July 16–19, 2020, at the Zuera circuit in Spain, followed by a second round at Portimão, Portugal on November 1, 2020 . These early events served as direct preparatory races for the Karting World Championship, establishing the series' role as a crucial developmental stepping stone for aspiring elite drivers . The inaugural champions of the series were Nikita Bedrin in the OK category, Arvid Lindblad in the OK-Junior category, Paolo Ippolito in the KZ2 category, and Dmitry Matveev in the 60 Mini category, setting a precedent for excellence within the organization .

## The Modern Ecosystem: Structure and Governance

The modern Champions of the Future is not a monolithic event but a sophisticated, multi-tiered ecosystem designed to capture and nurture talent across various stages of a racing career. This structure is built upon three core components: the flagship Champions of the Future Euro Series, the youth-focused Champions of the Future Academy Program (COTFA), and a burgeoning network of parallel series and future national championships . The entire operation is governed under the stringent regulations of the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) Karting, specifically through its Commission Internationale de Karting (CIK-FIA), which sanctions the series and ensures its alignment with global motorsport standards , . This formal sanctioning is a cornerstone of the series' legitimacy, placing it within the official hierarchy of karting and facilitating access to top-tier circuits and a pool of international competitors , . The series operates across eight distinct CIK-FIA classes, creating a comprehensive platform for drivers ranging from cadet-level juniors to senior professionals . This multi-faceted structure allows RGMMC to cater to different age groups and skill levels, creating a continuous talent pipeline from grassroots karting to the pinnacle of single-seater motorsport .

The Champions of the Future Euro Series stands as the premier component of the organization, functioning as the original and most prestigious part of the brand . Launched in 2020, it serves as an elite-tier developmental platform attracting top international drivers and teams , . In 2024 alone, the Euro Series drew a field of 215 drivers, underscoring its appeal and significance within the karting community . The series is structured around five meetings held between March and September, strategically located at renowned international circuits including PF International in England, Kristianstad in Sweden, the Slovakia Ring in Slovakia, and venues in France . This schedule provides drivers with a rigorous competitive calendar that mirrors the demands of higher-level motorsport. The Euro Series is explicitly described as a "must" for top international drivers and teams, highlighting its status as a critical preparatory series for the Karting World Championship , . This positioning solidifies its role as a vital link between junior karting categories and the ultimate goal of competing in Formula One and other upper echelons of motorsport . The series currently features several key classes, including OK, OK-Junior, KZ, KZ2, KZ2-Masters, OK-National, and OKN-Junior, providing a broad spectrum of competition for professional-level drivers .

Beyond the professional Euro Series, the Champions of the Future Academy Program (COTFA) represents a strategic evolution focused on grassroots development and inclusivity . Launched in March 2024, COTFA is a dedicated initiative designed to unearth talent worldwide at a young age , . It targets youth drivers in three distinct age-based categories: Mini 60 (ages 8–12), OK-N Junior (ages 12–14), and OK-N Senior (ages 14+ or 14–17/18 depending on the source) , , , . The program's design directly addresses two of the most significant challenges facing modern motorsport: cost and accessibility. By implementing a fixed-budget, 'arrive and drive' model, COTFA significantly lowers the financial barrier for young drivers and their families, making elite competition more inclusive , . All necessary equipment, including chassis, engines, and tires, is supplied by the promoter, ensuring equal competition for all participants regardless of their individual financial resources , . The inaugural round of the Academy Program took place at the Cremona International Circuit in Italy from March 27–31, 2024, attracting 33 nationalities and featuring driver caps of 36 per category, indicating strong initial interest , . Subsequent rounds have been held in Valencia, Spain, and Jesolo, Italy, with the 2025 season concluding at the Al Forsan International Sports Resort in Abu Dhabi, UAE , . This global footprint demonstrates the program's rapid expansion and its commitment to creating a truly international youth development platform , .

## The Champions of the Future Academy Program

The Champions of the Future Academy Program (COTFA) is a pivotal element of the RGMMC ecosystem, representing a deliberate and strategic focus on nurturing the next generation of motorsport talent while championing inclusivity . Launched in March 2024, COTFA is co-developed and supported by the F1 ACADEMY's 'Discover Your Drive' initiative, a collaboration that underscores its commitment to advancing female participation in motorsport . The program is structured into three mixed-gender categories based on age: Mini 60 for ages 8–12, OK-N Junior for ages 12–14, and OK-N Senior for ages 14+ , , . Each meeting is capped at 36 drivers per category, ensuring a high-quality, competitive environment . The inaugural European round at Cremona, Italy, saw intense demand, with the OK-N Junior category selling out and the other two categories nearing capacity, demonstrating the program's immediate success in attracting top young talent . The dual-race format at each event, consisting of two separate race days, each with Free Practice, Qualifying, two Qualifying Heats, and a Final, yields two podiums per category per meeting, maximizing competitive opportunities for the drivers .

A defining characteristic of the COTFA is its 'arrive and drive' model, which is central to its mission of increasing accessibility and inclusion , . Under this system, RGMMC provides all essential equipment, including Parolin or Kart Republic chassis, TM Kart or IAME engines, and Vega tires, which are distributed to teams via lottery , . This standardization of equipment ensures that competition is determined by driver skill rather than financial backing, leveling the playing field for participants from diverse economic backgrounds . The logistical backbone of the program is managed by DHL Motorsports, which transports over 22,000 parts for the 110 kart packages used in the inaugural event alone , . This comprehensive support package, which also includes fuel, tents, trolleys, and workbenches, allows young drivers to compete without the immense logistical and financial burden typically associated with motorsport . The program’s commitment to inclusion is further evidenced by record-breaking participation rates, with one event achieving a 30% female participation rate and producing the first-ever international-level trophy win by a female driver in the series' history . The partnership with the F1 ACADEMY amplifies this effort; the F1 ACADEMY sponsors three female drivers per category for each round, covering one-third of their season budget and providing them with branded karts and race suits . At the end of the 2024 season, the top three female drivers in the Seniors category are invited to an official F1 ACADEMY test, creating a tangible pathway from karting to the premier women's single-seater championship .

The leadership and personnel involved in the Academy Program further reinforce its connection to the wider world of elite motorsport. Key figures include RGMMC President James Geidel and F1 ACADEMY Managing Director Susie Wolff, whose collaboration is instrumental in talent identification and development . Susie Wolff, a former Formula One driver and advocate for diversity in motorsport, regularly attends COTFA events as a visible champion for the program . Moreover, experienced professionals from the F1 Academy, such as Isack Hadjar, serve as coaches, providing young talents with invaluable mentorship and linking them with established professionals . This synergy creates a powerful learning environment where cadet drivers can interact with and learn from athletes who are actively competing at the highest levels of the sport. The program's reach extends globally, with the 2025 season featuring rounds in Valencia, Spain, and Jesolo, Italy, and culminating in the UAE , . The 2026 calendar promises even greater expansion, with six rounds planned across Europe and the introduction of national series in the UAE, UK, and Macau, cementing COTFA's role as a cornerstone of global motorsport development . Live broadcasts of the events are available via Motorsport TV and YouTube, allowing a global audience to witness the emergence of future champions , .

## Expansion and Globalization Strategy

The Champions of the Future organization has pursued a clear and aggressive strategy of global expansion, moving beyond its origins in Europe to establish a presence in key international markets. This growth trajectory is evident in its detailed multi-year calendars and landmark partnerships, signaling a well-defined plan to become a truly global motorsport brand. A significant milestone in this strategy was the announcement of a partnership with K1, leading to the launch of 'Champions of the Future America' in 2026 . This marks the series' entry into the North American market, a region with a large and passionate motorsport fanbase. The inaugural season of Champions of the Future America will feature ten scheduled race rounds across K1 Circuit venues and Spring Mountain, commencing with an opening round from January 31–February 1, 2026 . The series will compete in Mini, IAME X30, KA100, and KZ classes, mirroring the structure of its European counterpart and providing a familiar yet exciting challenge for American drivers . This expansion into the United States is a strategic move to tap into a new talent pool and build a robust motorsport ecosystem in the region.

The 2026 calendar for the Champions of the Future Academy Program further illustrates the organization's geographic diversification and its commitment to building domestic motorsport infrastructure. Beyond the American expansion, the 2026 calendar includes six international rounds spread across Europe, Greece, and Oman, broadening the series' geographical footprint far beyond its traditional European heartlands . This diversification not only exposes drivers to a wider variety of circuits and climates but also enhances the series' global appeal. The 2026 international schedule includes rounds in Valencia, Spain (March); Thessaloniki, Greece (May); Viterbo, Italy (July); Oman (October); and a double-header finale at Al-Ain and Al Forsan in the UAE (November) . This extensive calendar demonstrates the logistical capability of RGMMC and the growing demand for the series' events worldwide.

Perhaps the most telling aspect of the globalization strategy is the planned introduction of national series in key markets. For 2026, Champions of the Future will launch a national series in the United Arab Emirates, running four rounds from February 20–22 at the Al Forsan circuit . Additionally, a new British national series is set to run four rounds between March and August 2026 . This model of establishing national championships is a proven method for building deep-rooted motorsport cultures and creating sustained talent pipelines within a country. By localizing the championship, RGMMC aims to foster greater brand loyalty and provide a clear, accessible pathway for domestic drivers to progress within the global Champions of the Future ecosystem. Further cementing its global ambitions, the series will make its debut in Macau in January 2026 with an event at the historic Coloane circuit . This expansion into Asia, a major hub for motorsport, demonstrates a sophisticated understanding of the global racing landscape and positions Champions of the Future as a truly international brand. ## Technical Regulations and Equipment Standardization

A foundational principle of the Champions of the Future series is its commitment to fostering equal competition through strict technical regulations and standardized equipment. This approach is central to its 'arrive and drive' philosophy, which aims to minimize the influence of private funding on performance and ensure that results are a true reflection of driver ability and team strategy , . Both the professional Champions of the Future Euro Series and the youth-focused Academy Program (COTFA) operate using identical or homologated equipment sets, governed by CIK-FIA specifications , . This uniformity is a deliberate strategy to level the playing field and increase the sport's accessibility for talented young drivers who may not have access to expensive private engineering resources . The use of standardized components removes a significant variable from the equation, shifting the focus entirely onto the skill of the driver, the quality of the pit crew, and the strategic acumen of the team management. This model is particularly effective in karting, where small differences in setup and tuning can have a profound impact on performance, and standardization helps to mitigate these variables.

The technical specifications for the karts used in the Champions of the Future series are meticulously defined to ensure parity and safety. For the younger categories in the Academy Program, the Mini 60 class utilizes Parolin chassis paired with TM engines, while the senior categories, OK-N Junior and OK-N Senior, employ Kart Republic chassis powered by IAME engines , . All equipment used is required to be CIK-FIA homologated, meaning it meets the rigorous safety and performance standards set by the international governing body for karting . Tyres are supplied by Vega, and all essential components are provided by the promoter, RGMMC, as part of the 'arrive and drive' package . This comprehensive provision of equipment is a key logistical achievement, handled by partners like DHL, which manages the transport of thousands of parts for each event . The distribution of this equipment is conducted via a lottery system, ensuring that every participant receives identical hardware for the weekend, thereby guaranteeing that no team has a technical advantage over another . This process reinforces the core values of fairness and equality that the series champions.

The following table outlines the standardized equipment used in the Champions of the Future series, illustrating the commitment to a level playing field across its various categories.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mini 60** | Parolin | TM Kart | Vega | Fuel, Tent, Trolley, Workbench, , |
| **OK-N Junior** | Kart Republic | IAME | Vega | Fuel, Tent, Trolley, Workbench, , |
| **OK-N Senior** | Kart Republic | IAME | Vega | Fuel, Tent, Trolley, Workbench, |

This strict adherence to technical regulations extends beyond just the choice of components. The series operates under the full suite of FIA Karting rules, which govern everything from vehicle dimensions and weight to engine displacement and safety requirements , . This ensures that drivers competing in Champions of the Future are prepared for the exacting standards they will face in other FIA-sanctioned events, including the Karting World Championship . By operating within this established regulatory framework, the series benefits from the collective experience and expertise of the global motorsport community, further enhancing its credibility and the value of its competition. The combination of standardized equipment, regulated trackside procedures, and a focus on fair play makes Champions of the Future a compelling proposition for drivers, teams, and fans alike, reinforcing its position as a premier developmental series in the world of motorsport.

## Notable Drivers and Achievements

While still a relatively young series, Champions of the Future has already cultivated a roster of talented drivers and achieved significant milestones that underscore its importance in the motorsport landscape. The inaugural champions of the series, crowned in 2020, set a high standard for future competitors. They include Nikita Bedrin in the OK category, Arvid Lindblad in the OK-Junior category, Paolo Ippolito in the KZ2 category, and Dmitry Matveev in the 60 Mini category . These early victories highlighted the series' ability to attract and identify top-tier talent at a young age. More recently, the Champions of the Future Academy Program has produced its own set of champions, showcasing the development pathway for youth drivers. The 2025 season concluded with Markas Silkunas (Lithuania) winning the OK-N Senior category, Conor Clancy (UAE) taking victory in the OK-N Junior category, Niccolo Perico (Italy) winning the Mini 60 category, and Wynn Godschalk (USA) claiming the Mini U10 title . These victories demonstrate the global nature of the talent pool that the series attracts, with winners hailing from multiple countries and continents.

One of the most significant achievements associated with the Champions of the Future Academy Program is its pioneering role in promoting gender equality in karting. The program has consistently reported high rates of female participation, reaching a record 30% in one of its events . This focus has translated into tangible success on the track, with the series producing the first-ever international-level trophy win by a female driver in its history . This accomplishment is a testament to the effectiveness of the series' inclusive model and its partnership with the F1 ACADEMY's 'Discover Your Drive' initiative, which actively supports and develops female talent . The program's emphasis on inclusion is further reflected in the diverse backgrounds of its participants. The inaugural European round at Cremona featured drivers from 33 different nationalities, highlighting the series' international character from its very first event . The 2025 Academy season continued this trend, with participants including Chiara Battig from Switzerland, Klara Kowalczyk from Poland, Ella Hakkinen from Monaco, Victoria Farfus from Brazil, and Atiqa Mir from India, among others . This rich tapestry of international representation is a key asset for the series, showcasing its role as a genuine global talent incubator.

The series has also attracted significant attention and involvement from key figures within the world of motorsport, further enhancing its profile and credibility. Susie Wolff, the Managing Director of the F1 ACADEMY, is a regular and vocal supporter of the Champions of the Future Academy Program, lending her considerable influence to its mission of inclusion and talent development , . Her presence at events serves as a powerful endorsement of the series' goals and provides young drivers with a direct connection to the highest levels of the sport . Similarly, experienced professionals like Isack Hadjar, a driver in the F1 Academy, have taken on coaching roles within the Academy Program, offering mentorship and practical guidance to the next generation of racers . This direct link between the karting academy and active F1 Academy professionals creates a seamless pathway for progression and enriches the learning experience for the cadet drivers. The following table lists some of the recent champions from the Champions of the Future Academy Program, providing concrete evidence of the series' competitive output and the global nature of its talent base.

| Category | Overall Champion | Nationality | Points Total (Season) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **OK-N Senior** | Markas Silkunas | Lithuania | 696 |
| **OK-N Junior** | Conor Clancy | United Arab Emirates | 519 |
| **Mini 60** | Niccolo Perico | Italy | 644 |
| **Mini U10** | Wynn Godschalk | USA | 520 |

To summarize, the achievements of Champions of the Future extend beyond mere race results. The series has successfully established itself as a credible and respected platform for developing motorsport talent. Its accomplishments in promoting female participation, attracting a diverse international field of competitors, and forging strategic partnerships with organizations like the F1 ACADEMY and logistics giant DHL collectively paint a picture of a dynamic, forward-thinking, and rapidly growing organization. As it continues its global expansion, the list of its champions and the successes of its alumni are expected to grow, further solidifying its reputation as a premier feeder series for the future stars of motorsport.

Live broadcasts of the Champions of the Future events are available via Motorsport TV and YouTube.
A significant milestone in the Champions of the Future's global expansion strategy was the announcement of a partnership with K1, leading to the launch of 'Champions of the Future America' in 2026.
The launch of 'Champions of the Future America' marks the series' entry into the North American market.
The inaugural season of Champions of the Future America will feature ten scheduled race rounds across K1 Circuit venues and Spring Mountain.
The inaugural season of Champions of the Future America will commence with an opening round from January 31–February 1, 2026.
The Champions of the Future America series will compete in Mini, IAME X30, KA100, and KZ classes.
The 2026 calendar for the Champions of the Future Academy Program includes six international rounds spread across Europe, Greece, and Oman.

The 2026 international schedule includes rounds in Valencia, Spain (March); Thessaloniki, Greece (May); Viterbo, Italy (July); Oman (October); and a double-header finale at Al-Ain and Al Forsan in the UAE (November).
For 2026, Champions of the Future will launch a national series in the United Arab Emirates.
The UAE national series will run four rounds from February 20–22 at the Al Forsan circuit.
A new British national series is set to run four rounds between March and August 2026.
The Champions of the Future series will make its debut in Macau in January 2026 with an event at the historic Coloane circuit.
Round 1 of the 2026 Champions of the Future Academy Program will be in Valencia, Spain, from March 6–8, 2026.
Round 2 of the 2026 Champions of the Future Academy Program will be in Thessaloniki, Greece, from May 29–31, 2026.
Round 3 of the 2026 Champions of the Future Academy Program will be in Viterbo, Italy, from July 17–19, 2026.
Round 4 of the 2026 Champions of the Future Academy Program will be in Oman from October 30–November 1, 2026.
Round 5 of the 2026 Champions of the Future Academy Program will be in Al-Ain, United Arab Emirates, from November 23–25, 2026.
Round 6 of the 2026 Champions of the Future Academy Program will be in Al Forsan, United Arab Emirates, from November 30–December 2, 2026.
The National Series Debut for Champions of the Future will be in Al Forsan, United Arab Emirates, from February 20–22, 2026.
A British National Series for Champions of the Future will run from March–August 2026.
The Macau Debut for Champions of the Future will be at Coloane Circuit from January 16–18, 2026.
A foundational principle of the Champions of the Future series is its commitment to fostering equal competition through strict technical regulations and standardized equipment.
The 'arrive and drive' philosophy aims to minimize the influence of private funding on performance.
The 'arrive and drive' philosophy aims to ensure that results are a true reflection of driver ability and team strategy.
Both the professional Champions of the Future Euro Series and the youth-focused Academy Program (COTFA) operate using identical or homologated equipment sets.
Equipment sets are governed by CIK-FIA specifications.
Uniformity of equipment is a deliberate strategy to level the playing field.
Uniformity of equipment is a deliberate strategy to increase the sport's accessibility for talented young drivers who may not have access to expensive private engineering resources.
The use of standardized components removes a significant variable from the equation.
The use of standardized components shifts the focus entirely onto the skill of the driver, the quality of the pit crew, and the strategic acumen of the team management.
For the younger categories in the Academy Program, the Mini 60 class utilizes Parolin chassis paired with TM engines.
The senior categories, OK-N Junior and OK-N Senior, employ Kart Republic chassis powered by IAME engines.
All equipment used is required to be CIK-FIA homologated.
CIK-FIA homologated equipment meets the rigorous safety and performance standards set by the international governing body for karting.
Tyres are supplied by Vega.
All essential components are provided by the promoter, RGMMC, as part of the 'arrive and drive' package.
The comprehensive provision of equipment is a key logistical achievement, handled by partners like DHL.
DHL manages the transport of thousands of parts for each event.
The distribution of equipment is conducted via a lottery system.
The lottery system ensures that every participant receives identical hardware for the weekend.
The lottery system guarantees that no team has a technical advantage over another.
The Mini 60 category uses Parolin chassis, TM Kart engines, and Vega tyres.
The Mini 60 category receives Fuel, Tent, Trolley, and Workbench as promoter support.
The OK-N Junior category uses Kart Republic chassis, IAME engines, and Vega tyres.
The OK-N Junior category receives Fuel, Tent, Trolley, and Workbench as promoter support.
The OK-N Senior category uses Kart Republic chassis, IAME engines, and Vega tyres.
The OK-N Senior category receives Fuel, Tent, Trolley, and Workbench as promoter support.
The series operates under the full suite of FIA Karting rules.
FIA Karting rules govern everything from vehicle dimensions and weight to engine displacement and safety requirements.
Drivers competing in Champions of the Future are prepared for the exacting standards they will face in other FIA-sanctioned events, including the Karting World Championship.
Nikita Bedrin was the inaugural champion of the Champions of the Future series in the OK category.
Arvid Lindblad was the inaugural champion of the Champions of the Future series in the OK-Junior category.
Paolo Ippolito was the inaugural champion of the Champions of the Future series in the KZ2 category.
Dmitry Matveev was the inaugural champion of the Champions of the Future series in the 60 Mini category.
The 2025 season of the Champions of the Future Academy Program concluded with Markas Silkunas (Lithuania) winning the OK-N Senior category.
Conor Clancy (UAE) took victory in the OK-N Junior category in the 2025 season of the Champions of the Future Academy Program.
Niccolo Perico (Italy) won the Mini 60 category in the 2025 season of the Champions of the Future Academy Program.
Wynn Godschalk (USA) claimed the Mini U10 title in the 2025 season of the Champions of the Future Academy Program.
The Champions of the Future Academy Program has consistently reported high rates of female participation, reaching a record 30% in one of its events.
The Champions of the Future Academy Program produced the first-ever international-level trophy win by a female driver in its history.
The Champions of the Future Academy Program's inclusive model and its partnership with the F1 ACADEMY's 'Discover Your Drive' initiative are effective in supporting female talent.
The inaugural European round at Cremona featured drivers from 33 different nationalities.
The 2025 Academy season included participants such as Chiara Battig from Switzerland, Klara Kowalczyk from Poland, Ella Hakkinen from Monaco, Victoria Farfus from Brazil, and Atiqa Mir from India.
Susie Wolff, the Managing Director of the F1 ACADEMY, is a regular and vocal supporter of the Champions of the Future Academy Program.
Susie Wolff lends her considerable influence to the Champions of the Future Academy Program's mission of inclusion and talent development.
Susie Wolff's presence at events serves as a powerful endorsement of the series' goals.
Susie Wolff's presence at events provides young drivers with a direct connection to the highest levels of the sport.
Experienced professionals like Isack Hadjar, a driver in the F1 Academy, have taken on coaching roles within the Academy Program.
Coaches like Isack Hadjar offer mentorship and practical guidance to the next generation of racers.

Niccolo Perico from Italy was the Overall Champion in the Mini 60 category with 644 points.
Wynn Godschalk from USA was the Overall Champion in the Mini U10 category with 520 points.

Minerva’s Virtual Academy offers bespoke education for racers aged 12 – 18. Unlike traditional schools, the Academy can be accessed anywhere in the world, at any time, and offers a world-class, flexible education fit for the 21st century. Pupils no longer have to miss school to attend training, track events, or race weekends.

The online school, which has won many awards since its launch, is run by Lawrence Tubb, a former head of department at Wycombe Abbey (one of the UK’s most prestigious private schools), and blends smart, interactive self-study (supported by the pupil’s personal mentor) with live online classes that can be managed around the athletes’ schedule. Young racers in particular are assisted by a unique mentoring programme that helps to develop them professionally as well as academically, overseeing their mental wellbeing whilst teaching soft skills such as public-speaking, self-confidence, and self-discipline.

Its pupils, who are able to choose from over 20 subjects at GCSE or A Level, are welcomed into a thriving, global community of talented pupils in sport and the arts, including Olympic hopefuls, West End performers, musicians, actors, and social media influencers, setting them up with brilliant friendships and connections for later on in life.

For the most bespoke solution (very popular in karting), private tutors from the school provide 1-2-1 teaching either in person or online, to ensure the pupil receives maximum attention and support on their path to success.

**Champions of the Future** (**COTF**) is a [kart racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_racing "Kart racing") competition organised by the RGMMC Group and sanctioned by [FIA Karting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_Karting "FIA Karting") (CIK-FIA). Founded in 2020, COTF is one of 11 competitions on the [international kart racing calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_kart_racing_championships#Active_international_championships "List of kart racing championships") in [CIK-FIA classes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_Internationale_de_Karting#Categories "Commission Internationale de Karting"). Initially a two-round series in [OK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2") and [OK-Junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-Junior "OK-Junior") (OK-J)—with single-round finals in [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2") and [60 Mini](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=60_Mini&action=edit&redlink=1 "60 Mini (page does not exist)")—the championship has since expanded to all eight CIK-FIA classes across the: **Euro Series** ([OK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2"), [OK-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF3 "KF3")), **Shifters** ([KZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_/(karting/) "KZ (karting)"), [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2"), [KZ2-M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2-M "KZ2-M")), and **Academy Program** ([OK-N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-N "OK-N"), [OKN-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OKN-J "OKN-J"), [60 Mini](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=60_Mini&action=edit&redlink=1 "60 Mini (page does not exist)")), the latter supported by [F1 Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F1_Academy "F1 Academy"). COTF also hosted the one-off **Winter Series** at [Franciacorta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autodromo_di_Franciacorta "Autodromo di Franciacorta") in 2022. COTF is set to expand to national series in 2026, hosting a British title with [Motorsport UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorsport_UK "Motorsport UK"), an [Emirati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") title, a [Macanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macau "Macau") title, and an [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") title. The Euro Series and Shifters events traditionally take place in the two weeks prior to a [World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship "Karting World Championship") or [European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_European_Championship "Karting European Championship") round at the same [circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_circuit "Kart circuit"). Notable former champions include [Nikita Bedrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Bedrin "Nikita Bedrin") (2020, OK), [Arvid Lindblad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arvid_Lindblad "Arvid Lindblad") (2020, OK-J), [Rafael Câmara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_C%C3%A2mara "Rafael Câmara") (2021, OK), [Freddie Slater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Slater_/(racing_driver/) "Freddie Slater (racing driver)") (2021, OK-J), [Alex Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Powell "Alex Powell") (2023, OK), and [Dries Van Langendonck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dries_Van_Langendonck "Dries Van Langendonck") (2024, OK-J). [Luna Fluxá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_Flux%C3%A1 "Luna Fluxá") (2024, OK-N) is the only [female driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_racing_drivers "List of female racing drivers") to win a title. ### Background (1962–2019) \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Champions_of_the_Future&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Background (1962–2019)")\] [![Image 11: The pre-grid of the 2015 KZ World Championship at Le Mans](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/KZ_PREGRID_KSP_6_7810-edit-660x330.jpg/250px-KZ_PREGRID_KSP_6_7810-edit-660x330.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KZ_PREGRID_KSP_6_7810-edit-660x330.jpg) The RGMMC Group has been the official [promoter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promoter_/(entertainment/) "Promoter (entertainment)") of [CIK-FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA "CIK-FIA") events—the [World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship "Karting World Championship") and [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_European_Championship "Karting European Championship") Championships—since 2018. The [Commission Internationale de Karting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_Internationale_de_Karting "Commission Internationale de Karting") (CIK-FIA) was founded in 1962 by the [Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_de_l%27Automobile "Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile") (FIA) to govern the rising international sport of [kart racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_racing "Kart racing").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-1) The inaugural [CIK-FIA World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA_World_Championship "CIK-FIA World Championship") was hosted two years later at the _[Pista d'Oro](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pista_d%27Oro&action=edit&redlink=1 "Pista d'Oro (page does not exist)")_ in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome"), which again held the event in 1965.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-2) The CIK-FIA began its [homologation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologation_/(motorsport/) "Homologation (motorsport)") of distinct classes in the discipline in 1974, when the first 125 cc [gearbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gearbox "Gearbox") category was created for the [European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_European_Championship "Karting European Championship"): [Formula C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_/(karting/) "KZ (karting)") when [Formula Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF1 "KF1") was introduced to control technical evolutions and costs.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-4) The direct-drive classes were adapted in 1981, when the 135 cc [Formula K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_K "Formula K") (FK), 100 cc [Intercontinental "OK-N") and [OKN-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OKN-J "OKN-J")) and €23,000 (60 Mini),[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-AP2024-43) including a new (TT), qualifying heats (QH), super heats (SH), and the finals:[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-77) * Thursday: FP + TT (morning), QH (afternoon); * Friday: warm-up + QH; * Saturday: warm-up + SH (morning), [OK-J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK-J "OK-J") and [OK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2") final (afternoon). The Euro Series follows the general [CIK-FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA "CIK-FIA") points system, with a maximum of: 25 for QH, 25 for SH, and 50 for finals; [dead heats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_heat "Dead heat") are settled via [count-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_motorsport_terms#C "Glossary of motorsport terms") in finals.[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-78)[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-FIA2025-79) As of 2025, Shifters is held over a three-day weekend composed of free practice (FP), qualifying practice (QP), qualifying heats (QH), super heats (SH), and the finals:[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champions_of_the_Future#cite_note-80) * Thursday: FP (morning), QP (afternoon); * Friday: warm-up + QH; * Saturday: warm-up + SH (morning), [KZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_/(karting/) "KZ (karting)") and [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2") final (afternoon). RGMMC, K1 team up to create 'Champions of the Future America'
=============================================================

Advertisement

RGMMC Group, a global leader in international karting promotion and the organization behind the highly acclaimed 'Champions of the Future' series, has announced a landmark partnership with K1 to launch Champions of the Future America, a new initiative designed to elevate the next generation of American motorsport talent and create new pathways through the sport.

This collaboration marks a major milestone in bringing a new format of competitive karting platform to the U.S. market, giving young American drivers access to the same professional standards, organization, technology, and competitive environment that have helped shape numerous current elite motorsport athletes.

“America is the largest karting market, and partnering with K1 allows us to bring a proven development pathway to a country with passion, scale, and talent. While bridging the gap between Europe and the United States,” said James Geidel, CEO of RGMMC.

K1, a recognized leader in American karting and motorsport entertainment since 2003 with brands K1 Speed and K1 Circuit, will bring its national footprint, industry knowledge, and strong community of young racers to the partnership. Together, RGMMC and K1 will introduce a series of events and programs focused on doing things differently.

“K1’s ambition is to introduce casual indoor go-kart racers to the world of outdoor karting as part of the pathway to professional motorsport,” said K1’s Founder and CEO, David Danglard. “By partnering with Champions of the Future in North America, we can achieve this goal and give our drivers the best opportunity to pursue their racing dreams.”

Champions of the Future America will feature:

● A professionally organized race series aligned with international standards

● Pathways for U.S. drivers to access global karting competitions

● State-of-the-art event management and technological support

The first events are set to launch in 2026, with full details to be released shortly Rd 1 January 31- February 1 K1 Circuit Rd 2 February 28 -March 1 K1 Circuit Rd 3 March 21- 22 K1 Circuit Rd 4 April 18-19 K1 Circuit Rd 5 & 6 May 29-31 Spring Mountain Double header 3 Day Event Rd 7 June 27-28 K1 Circuit Rd 8 July 18-19 K1 Circuit Rd 9 August 29-30 K1 Circuit Rd 10 September 19-20 K1 Circuit Categories to be included: Mini, IAME X30, KA100, and KZ classes.

Those interested can sign up for updates [here](https://www.k1circuit.com/champions-of-the-future-america).

**Our nine F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE supported karters returned to action for Round 2 of the 2025 Champions of the Future Academy Program campaign.**

Heading to the Kartodromo Internacional Lucas Guerro, the karters soon got to grips with the Valencian circuit’s high-speed and technical configuration, with Seniors’ Chiara Battig and Klara Kowalczyk fighting hard against each other in a last-lap podium battle.

### MINI 60 (8 TO 11 YEARS OLD)

Alba Cueva was quickest out of the box on Day 1, qualifying in P6 and battling hard throughout both Heats to earn herself a P7 start for the Final. The Spanish karter would line up behind Ava Lawrence who fought back after a difficult Qualifying only resulted in a 14th place finish. The Emirati racer steadily made up four places in each Heat, with her consistency being rewarded with a spot on the third row.

Atiqa Mir faced her own challenges in the Heats after a promising P10 result in Qualifying. Losing ground in the fierce battles, she was classified in P15 and P17 respectively, which resulted in a P17 start for the Final.

Both Lawrence and Cueva dropped back slightly in the middle stint but ended up being classified where they started inside the top-seven. Mir clawed back three places on track and was promoted up one place following a post-race penalty for the race winner.

![Image 1: Mir fought hard to deliver points in both Finals](https://res.cloudinary.com/prod-f2f3/ar_16:9,c_fill,dpr_1.0,f_auto,g_auto,h_563,w_1000/v1/FA/Global/articles/2025/04_April/2025_CotFA_Valencia_Sa2_394_ARNAU_VI%C3%91ALS)

Mir fought hard to deliver points in both Finals

Day 2 got off to a positive note with a strong Qualifying performances from Lawrence in P6. Pushing on ahead across both Heats, the Emirati karter made up four places to secure a top-four start for the Final. Losing out slightly, she finished seventh overall, crucially keeping her inside the top-eight in the Standings.

Cueva might have qualified behind Lawrence initially, but the Spaniard would ultimately end the weekend ahead after converting her P6 start for the Final into a top-six finish. The second day proved to be more difficult for Mir, but she managed to make progress after Day 1’s challenges. Qualifying in P19, the Indian karter cut her way through to bring home a P13 finish in the Final.

### OK-N JUNIOR (11 TO 14 YEARS OLD)

Victoria Farfus led the charge from the trio in the OK-N Junior category, securing a top-five spot in the Time Qualifying session, one place ahead of Angelina Simons. The Brazilian’s pace continued to look strong across both Heats, jumping into P4 on the opening lap of the first Heat. After dropping back to P7 the following lap, Farfus eventually settled for a P6 finish, following that up with a P5 in Heat 2, which awarded her a spot on the third row for the Final.

[READ MORE: Career Spotlight: Meet Hannah Prydderch, Content Editor at F1 ACADEMY](https://www.f1academy.com/Latest/2uesjCaY0pZoVQLxgnjhmK/career-spotlight-meet-hannah-prydderch-content-editor-at-f1-academy)

Meanwhile, Simons found herself facing two tough Heats. Forced to retire early from Heat 1 on Lap 4, the Spaniard dropped six places in the second Heat, leaving her to start the Final from P23. Vanesa Silkunaite struggled to match the pair’s pace in Qualifying, finishing 17th overall. However, the Lithuanian quickly made up for lost ground, cutting through the pack to finish P11 and P9 in the Heats, gifting her an eighth-place start.

In the Final, Farfus had the podium in her sights as she put the pressure on, making up two places in the melee early on. Stuck in a four-kart train, she lost fourth with three laps to go before a brief trip over the run-off at Turns 15 and 16 gave Silkunaite a chance to get through for fifth. This subsequently turned into a top-four finish after a penalty was awarded to the third-place finisher.

Simons also mounted a comeback, surviving a chaotic opening lap to claw her way back up from P23 to P9. However, she was later demoted to P15 due to a 5-second penalty for a technical infringement.

![Image 2: Simons kept fighting on after enduring some tough Heats in Valencia](https://res.cloudinary.com/prod-f2f3/ar_16:9,c_fill,dpr_1.0,f_auto,g_auto,h_563,w_1000/v1/FA/Global/articles/2025/04_April/2025_CotFA_Valencia_Sa1_148_ARNAU_VI%C3%91ALS)

Simons kept fighting on after enduring some tough Heats in Valencia

The Spaniard was the initially the fastest in the trio on Day 2, qualifying fourth for the Heats. Whilst losing three places in Heat 1 was a setback, Heat 2 would prove more disastrous as she was forced to retire after a chaotic opening corner. Determined to fight back from P19, she cut through the mid-pack to secure a P5 finish to round out her weekend.

Farfus and Silkunaite also struggled off the bat, qualifying in P15 and P28 respectively. Farfus bounced back in the Heats to put herself on the third row for the Final. Getting stuck into the battles, the Brazilian narrowly missed out on a podium by six tenths. Silkunaite also made inroads, improving by a combined 22 places across both Heats.

[READ MORE: In-Season Testing Round-Up: What we learnt from three days of running in Jeddah](https://www.f1academy.com/Latest/15imhamR1pHwhll5z1aypg/in-season-testing-round-up-what-we-learnt-from-three-days-of-running-in)

Unable to match the same progress in the Final, the Lithuanian karter did manage to make up five places to P11 to keep her towards the top end of the Standings in P6, with Farfus joining her inside the top-10.

### OK-N SENIOR (14 TO 17 YEARS OLD)

Chiara Battig’s strong form from the opening round continued into Valencia as the Swiss driver turned a P4 result in Qualifying into a front row start for the Final, finishing both Heats in second.

Not far behind, Klara Kowalczyk and Ella Hakkinen each qualified inside the top-10 and tried to push their way up the order. Despite a tricky Heat 1 for Kowalczyk, the Polish racer managed to hold on to the seventh-place spot on the Final grid. Hakkinen was able to make more progress, gaining eight places across the two Heats to line up just behind Battig in third.

![Image 3: Battig left delivered her second podium of the year on Day 2 with Kowalczyk right in third](https://res.cloudinary.com/prod-f2f3/ar_16:9,c_fill,dpr_1.0,f_auto,g_auto,h_563,w_1000/v1/FA/Global/articles/2025/04_April/RGMMC_13-04-25_frnetwork-35_ARNAU_VI%C3%91ALS)

Battig (left) delivered her second podium of the year on Day 2 with Kowalczyk (right) in third

Unfortunately for Battig, the race start didn’t go according to plan. Getting squeezed by the pack into the opening corner, she tumbled down the order to P19 by the end of the first lap. Remaining undeterred by the setback, Battig picked her way through the field and recovered to a top-10 finish.

With Hakkinen falling back to P7, it was up to Kowalczyk to take advantage of the battles around her. Making her way into fourth, the Pole was chasing a podium but couldn’t quite get close enough to the silverware with Hakkinen making up lost ground to round out the top-five.

[READ MORE: INSIDE STORY: Behind the scenes of Joanne Ciconte's rollercoaster debut weekend in F1 ACADEMY](https://www.f1academy.com/Latest/1H21o89bY4YKdI9bilxQ8I/inside-story-behind-the-scenes-of-joanne-cicontes-rollercoaster-debut)

The hunt for the podium kicked up a notch on Day 2 with Battig and Kowalczyk qualifying inside the top-four. The Swiss karter’s impressive form in the Heats paid off as Battig lined up on pole for the Final, with the Pole just behind her in third. Although neither could take home the win, they were locked in a fierce last-lap showdown to determine the podium positions, with Battig eventually sealing second.

Hakkinen may have qualified a little bit further back in P8, but the Monegasque karter would end up only two tenths back from the podium by the Final chequered flag. A successful weekend for the trio has kept them all within the top-10 in the Standings, with Battig leading the way in P3 followed by Kowalczyk in P7 and Hakkinen in ninth.

The 2025 COTFA season continues in the summer with a visit to Jesolo, Italy from July 4-6. To see the full list of results from Round 2 and to view the remaining rounds on the calendar, visit the COTFA website [here](https://www.championskartingacademy.com/).

Published: 07 February 2025

Columns: Close Up

In a constantly evolving landscape, the FIA motorsport ladder is strengthening the connection between grassroots categories and the highest levels of competition. The Champions of the Future Academy Program, now entering its second full season, fits into this scenario with an innovative model based on inclusion, cost efficiency, and equal competition opportunities.

**A growth model for motorsport**  
The Champions of the Future Academy program has quickly gained a prominent role in the motorsport scene. In a sector where the connection between karting and Formula 1 is becoming increasingly direct, the initiative promoted by RGMMC stands out due to several key factors: inclusion, controlled costs through a fixed budget, and fair competition, ensured by the use of identical equipment for all participants.

**Expanding beyond traditional boundaries**  
One of the program’s most innovative aspects is the geographical expansion of karting, bringing the discipline to countries where motorsport is rapidly growing. This ambitious effort, successfully managed by the RGMMC team, has contributed to a broader dissemination of the sport and created new opportunities for young talents.

![Image 1](https://www.vroomkart.com/sites/vroomkart.com/files/ckeditor/images/FB.png)

**Female inclusion in Motorsport**  
The Academy has also achieved significant results in terms of female participation. For the first time, an international-level trophy was won by a female driver, and women now make up 30% of the participants. This concrete achievement reflects a real shift beyond mere discussions about the role of women in motorsport.

![Image 2](https://www.vroomkart.com/sites/vroomkart.com/files/ckeditor/images/RBAV_241204_COTFA_ALFORSAN_5347-scaled.jpg)

**A broad foundation for a competitive Future**  
The program aims to make motorsport more accessible by increasing the number of participants. This approach is already showing results, supported by key figures such as Susie Wolff, whose consistent presence at events serves as a strong incentive for young female drivers.

**Equal conditions in competition**  
The world of karting has undergone significant changes in recent years, with the “arrive and drive” model becoming the standard. In this context, RGMMC has created a fair competitive environment where drivers can showcase their talent without having to switch teams to remain competitive. This setup helps young drivers develop the ability to maximize their available resources, an essential skill for those aiming for higher levels.

![Image 3](https://www.vroomkart.com/sites/vroomkart.com/files/ckeditor/images/isack-hadjar2.jpg)

#### Isack Hadjar was present as a coach in Dubai

**Inspiration from the Champions of the Future**  
The presence of drivers from higher categories, such as Formula 2 and the F1 Academy, in the paddock serves as an additional source of motivation for young talents. Figures like Isack Hadjar provide practical advice and share their experiences, creating a direct bridge between the new generation and industry professionals.
